title: A Block of Length Two or More With Sum Divisible by k

concept.title: The earliest index of each remainder
body: Now the block must have at least **two** elements. Two prefix sums with the same remainder enclose a block whose sum is divisible by `k`, but the block has the right length only if the two prefixes are **at least 2 positions apart**. So store the **earliest** index of each remainder and compare distances.
Do not overwrite the stored index of a remainder when you see it again: the earliest position gives the longest block and so the best chance to reach length 2.

statement: Is there a block of at least two consecutive elements whose sum is divisible by `k` (a sum of 0 counts)? Print `yes` or `no`.

examples.note: The sums of the blocks of two or more elements are 25, 8 and 31, none a multiple of 6.

hints: Equal remainders of two prefix sums mean a good block between them.
The block needs at least two elements, so the prefixes must be at least 2 apart.
Store only the first index of each remainder.

explanation: The earliest index of each remainder gives the longest block; it only has to be at least two elements long.
solution.complexity: Time O(n) on average, space O(min(n, k)).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, k = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

first = {0: -1}
prefix = 0
found = False
for i in range(n):
    prefix += a[i]
    rem = prefix % k
    if rem in first:
        if i - first[rem] >= 2:
            found = True
            break
    else:
        first[rem] = i
print("yes" if found else "no")
